articles.title: Uganda Key Message Update: Crisis (IPC Phase 3) to persist in Karamoja; deterioration expected in refugee camps, September 2026 - January 2027
articles.description: Country: Uganda Source: Famine Early Warning System Network Please refer to the attached file. Key Messages In Karamoja, Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected to persist through January , driven by low livestock ownership among poor households and widespread crop losses following severely below-average rainfall through the second half of the March-October rainy season. Poor temporal rainfall distribution and below-average totals from June onward also negatively affected late-planted crops such as beans, green grams, sweet potatoes, and cassava. In some areas, farmers planted up to three times, with crops repeatedly failing to germinate. Most poor households are unable to meet their minimum food needs without engaging in unsustainable coping methods, despite a widespread one-time distribution of humanitarian food assistance in August. To reduce income gaps, households are engaging in off-own-farm activities, including gold mining, and those with livestock have increased sales, particularly of small ruminants and poultry. However, the income from these revenue streams is insufficient to fully mitigate food consumption gaps. Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes persisted in most northern Uganda refugee settlements in September, and Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are expected across all refugee camps between October and January . As first season food stocks deplete among the poorest refugee households and food prices increase in line with typical seasonal trends, humanitarian food assistance will become insufficient to offset the growing gap in food access. Refugee households will seek agricultural labor opportunities during the second season rains to help narrow income gaps, but face high competition from host communities. According to WFP, as of late August, assistance is currently funded to continue at current levels through December. As of September 30, funding for food assistance in 2027 had received only about 33 percent of the required funding . In September, the typical onset of the second season rains in Uganda’s bimodal areas, rainfall ranged from -25 to -100 mm below average across the country. However, El Niño-driven heavy rainfall is forecast from October to December, which is expected to bring cumulatively above-average total rainfall for the season. The below average rainfall further diminished prospects for recovery of late-planted first season crops in Karamoja. In central and southwestern bimodal areas, prolonged dry spells that began towards the end of April, coupled with atypically high temperatures, have led to wilting and scorching of coffee trees , with coffee quality and yields expected to decline by about 10 percent . The most affected districts include greater Masaka, Kyotera, Sembabule, and Luwero. Although some rainfall returned in September, it came too late to reverse the extensive damage to coffee and food crops, including bananas, which will continue to strain household food access and income, particularly in central and western Uganda. In addition, coffee prices have fallen sharply by 14.5 percent due to increased global supply amid prolonged dry conditions and declining export volumes. The decreases in yield, quality, and price are expected to result in lower incomes for households in these regions. Along the cattle corridor extending from southwestern to northeastern Uganda, restrictions on livestock movement and trade in districts such as Nakasongola were intensified in September as part of ongoing effort to contain Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD). The ban on the movement and sale of livestock and meat, particularly along key transit routes in Nakasongola District, has disrupted household livelihoods by reducing both food and income access. At the same time, the livestock sector continues to face the adverse effects of prolonged abnormal dryness, which has reduced pasture and water availability. The deteriorating livestock conditions have also led to a sharp decline in milk production,with daily output reportedly dropping from about 40,000 liters to less than 1,000 liters per day in districts such as Kasese. In Karamoja, despite generally adequate pasture conditions, low water availability has begun to drive atypically early seasonal livestock migrations which typically begin in November. Increased demand for USD to finance fuel imports amid a growing trade deficit contributed to UGX depreciation of 4–5 percent from late August to mid-September, and elevated fuel prices and currency depreciation put upward pressure on transport and food import costs. Inflation for food crops and related items rose from 1.2 percent in August to 7.0 percent in September, while energy, fuel and utilities (EFU) inflation rose from 0.2 percent in August to 0.5 percent in September. Fuel prices in Uganda remained slightly higher than in neighboring countries, with gasoline retailing at about 6,529 UGX per liter.The rise in staple food prices is driven in part by the elevated fuel costs, but also typical seasonal depletion of domestically-produced stocks and atypically high regional demand from Kenya, South Sudan, Rwanda, and the DRC. Bean prices increased by 6.3 percent by mid-September, up from 2.4 percent in August, and both sorghum and maize remained elevated. Cassava and cooking bananas also recorded high prices. Bananas increased to 16 percent from 8.4 percent in August. Other food crops with elevated prices include sweet potatoes, milk, and fruits.

articles.title: Transcript: Trump Tirade over Shrinking Rally Crowds Emasculates MAGA
articles.description: The following is a lightly edited transcript of the October 6 episode of the Daily Blast podcast. Listen to it here . Greg Sargent: This is The Daily Blast from The New Republic , produced and presented by the DSR Network. I’m your host, Greg Sargent. Donald Trump has been holding rallies lately to energize his voters for the midterms, but he’s running into problems. Press scrutiny of his declining crowd sizes has been harsh, and he exploded in a crazed rant over this, fuming that in fact his rallies are “HOTTER” than ever. But if anything, these rallies are an admission of weakness and failure. Republicans themselves are leaking word that Trump’s campaigning is a signal of the midterm emergency the GOP faces in deep red areas. And one rally in Ohio displayed a scene that’s doubly revealing along these lines. We’re getting into all of this with Salon’s Amanda Marcotte, a skilled interpreter of MAGA, who has a good piece on Trump’s epic but failing struggle to make voters like him. Amanda, always good to have you on. Amanda Marcotte: Thanks for having me. Sargent: So Trump has done rallies in Ohio, Oklahoma, Alabama, and Texas, and he’s doing one Monday night in Nebraska. The Times had two pieces showing his crowd size is diminishing considerably. In Alabama, the Times reports , upper sections were, quote, “almost completely empty,” in an arena that’s smaller than previous ones. And there were empty sections at an even smaller arena in Ohio, the Times noted . Amanda, even more to the point, polls are showing Republicans turning on him in spite of all these efforts. Your thoughts on all that? Marcotte: Yeah, I think it’s twofold. I think obviously he’s aging, he’s getting even weaker. The political situation is so embarrassing right now that even his loyal supporters are beginning to be uncomfortable. We are hitting that same portion of, like, Bush’s second term, where even his voters just didn’t want to defend him anymore. It feels, I think, for a lot of the people that support him, it feels kind of pointless at this point. Like, so much of the reason that a lot of Trump supporters kept doubling down and doubling down and doubling down was that they wanted to never admit they were wrong to liberals, first of all. And second of all, as long as this political project had legs and they could kind of keep reviving the corpse and pushing into the future, it had value to them. So there was a purpose behind blind loyalty. But you can’t reelect Trump. It’s not worth it anymore, now that he’s a lame duck and there’s only so much juice they can squeeze out of this lemon. Sargent: So Trump raged wildly at the Times for questioning his crowd sizes. He posted on Truth Social that his Ohio rally was “great” and “PACKED,” in all caps. He accused the Times of dishonesty. And he said this about his rallies: “The rallies are HOTTER than ever. The networks refuse under any circumstances to show the crowds, but you can hear the thunderous applause, and you know that it represents thousands and thousands of people.” He also said: “I never have empty seats, never have and never will.” Amanda, I don’t know, for someone who’s doing so smashingly well, Trump sounds awfully angry and unhappy. Your thoughts about that? Marcotte: I mean, wasn’t it at one of these rallies he literally got up and said that he knows more about every subject on the planet, on the whole planet, than any other person knows about anything? When you’re standing there being like, I’m the greatest of all time, and to a half-empty crowd—it’s like the trope on television when somebody says something and then comically they get disproven the next minute. Sargent: And on top of that, this actually gets at a real thing, which is that in three of these states that he’s held rallies in, there really are tough Senate races—Texas, Ohio, and even Nebraska, which has somehow become closer now. In fact, one GOP lawmaker from a state Trump recently visited told CNN, quote, “this is a five-alarm fire.” Amanda, the five-alarm fire is among MAGA and Republican voters. Obviously, the internal data is showing cratering support among Republican voters, especially MAGA ones. The Fox poll of Texas actually showed non-MAGA Republicans not approving of Trump. Like, more non-MAGA Republicans disapprove of Trump than approve of him. Marcotte: I think it’s also true that they have this perception, and I don’t think it’s incorrect, that whatever Trumpism is, was, and whatever they got out of it, that’s coming to an end. And no one wants to be the last person at a party, right? Sargent: Right. Right. I think that’s a real dynamic for sure. Marcotte: Yeah. And I think that it’s not unreasonable for people that saw Donald Trump as their pathway to the kind of culture war victories that they were hoping to get, many of which they did—deportations, abortion bans coming back, you know, homophobia has been surging back, that sort of thing. I mean, they got a lot of victories. Open racism has been normalized again. So they did get a lot of victories. And now he’s just this embarrassment. He got them into this war, he’s ruining the economy. He’s a lame duck. So this is a good time to sort of do an Irish exit. Sargent: At this rally in Ohio, Trump talked about how Haitian immigrants who used to get temporary protected status are now getting deported. And he lied about how they’ve hurt the town of Springfield. In fact, the Haitian influx has done a lot to help reinvigorate the place. Immigrants have reinvigorated the left-behind heartland in many ways, the places where Americans, especially young Americans, have deserted. But that aside, the crowd got very excited when Trump said the Haitians are getting sent back to their home country, where the conditions are horrific. They started to chant : “deport, deport.�� Amanda, before we get to the culture war stuff here, they get mad when people like us say that the lifeblood of MAGA is sadism, but there you have it on full display. That is the lifeblood of MAGA. Marcotte: Yeah. And I think the reason that Trump rallies have been as popular as they are, even though it’s the same thing over and over again, is precisely this. There’s safety in numbers. I think a lot of the people that have this sadistic desire to inflict pain on women, minorities, LGBTQ people—they don’t necessarily feel comfortable saying that on an individual basis. But when they go to a rally, they can chant hateful, racist things like that and get that glee, and they’re kind of anonymous. Sargent: They’re actually kind of losing the culture wars over immigration, in a certain sense. And I think this Ohio scene displayed it in an interesting way. The New York Times had some polls over the weeken d of these Senate races. Just going to read the top lines. James Talarico, the Democrat, is ahead in Texas, 51 to 45. Mary Peltola is ahead in Alaska, 50 to 43, also the Democrat. In Ohio, Sherrod Brown is up three points. In Iowa, Josh Turek, the Democrat, is down one. And Kansas is tied, which is incredible. But here’s the thing I want to get to. In all these states, Donald Trump is underwater on immigration. That means that among likely voters, more than half disapprove of his performance on immigration. Again, this is in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, and Texas. All states Trump won by double digits. And get this: the percentages who strongly disapprove are in the forties in all these states. I have not seen numbers like this before. I mean, he has completely lost the deep red states on his best issue. And here you’ve got, like, a bunch of MAGA people in a bubble chanting the words “deport, deport, deport,” thinking that they’re winning this debate in some sense. But in reality it’s just crushing Republicans, even in these red states. What do you make of all that? Marcotte: After the shootings in Minneapolis, I felt like this was probably going to—I’m surprised at how much it has turned around, but I felt like this was going to happen. Thomas Edsall in The New York Times had a really good article recently where he shared some research that showed that while Republican voters have become kind of more racist under Trump, the opposite has happened to Democratic voters. Which is to say, I think they’ve had to think about some of these issues a little bit more than they used to, and they’ve discussed them. And I think their racial tolerance levels have gone up in response. And that’s an interesting thing. And I suspect that’s happening kind of in the center too, where a lot of people who had a delusion about this country’s racism and had convinced themselves it wasn’t that serious are seeing this happen, and they’re finally admitting that, like, Haitians are just, like, normal people that want to work hard and raise their families, you know? Sargent: Yeah, absolutely. I do want to point out, though, that there’s a little bit of cause for optimism in this. Because if you’ve got majorities in these states that Trump carried by double digits turning against Trump on immigration, what it means is that the people that were chanting “deport, deport, deport” kind of represent an increasingly fringe minority. The MAGA sadism is a minority position at this point, even in some of these red states. And it’s kind of creating this opening for Democrats to capture some of these much softer Republicans and Republican-leaning independents who are horrified by what they’re seeing, don’t relish it the way the MAGA sadists do, and could potentially be looking for something else. I think there’s potentially cause for real gains to be made there, in terms of building a larger consensus kind of in favor of immigration. What do you think? Marcotte: Yeah, I think absolutely. And I think it’s moments like this that you can actually start to change people’s minds, right? The door has been cracked open. You know, they took it so far that they’re causing some people that otherwise were kind of softly racist towards immigrants to feel bad, and to maybe reconsider some of the opinions they had. Sargent: For MAGA, Trump’s promise was that he would defeat us, right? He would crush you and me, basically. He would crush liberal America, you know, destroy us culturally, rout us in the culture wars permanently, put America back on a anti-woke path, or whatever the precise thing they want is. But that hasn’t happened, right? It’s not happening, in the sense that majorities are rejecting him on immigration. They’re rejecting the white nationalism. And, you know, their candidates are in trouble in very deep red areas as a result of this. And so maybe the fact that liberal America is fighting back and is mobilizing and is so energized and is really ready to take this all the way, right—take this to the mat, as it were—is itself a dissuading factor for some of these MAGA Republicans. They say, well, OK, you know, he’s not actually crushing them. He’s not crushing Amanda Marcotte and Greg Sargent, or whatever. You know what I mean? He’s not crushing those libs. So I don’t know, man, I’m not sure I’m on this train anymore. Does that seem crazy? Marcotte: No, that’s really perceptive. I love it. I love it. That’s amazing. Because it’s like—you’re right, like, many broken promises from Trump. He’s going to lower prices. He’s going to keep us out of wars. He’s going to crush the libs. Add that to the list of broken promises. I love it. And yeah, I think, you know, it also just—there was that one moment, like right after he won, for a few months, where there was this sense that MAGA was, like, culturally ascendant. And it started to crack apart, right? Basically right when Charlie Kirk died, honestly. And like, Jimmy Kimmel—they tried to fire him, and instead it showed, like, there was this support for Jimmy Kimmel. And I think at that point they began to realize that actually most Americans still think that they are not cool, and they will never be cool. And I think that that’s been a shot in the arm culturally for the left, and has been very depressing for the right. And you love to see it. Sargent: Well, you know what else happened at around the time when that supposed cultural ascendancy seemed to suddenly waver and start tailspinning down? Two things. Kilmar Abrego Garcia was sent to a foreign torture prison, and ICE started invading cities. I think that really was one of the things that started the unraveling. Marcotte: Yeah, no, I mean, part of what MAGA was able to do to sort of make themselves seem cool, even for a minute, was they presented their fascist ideas as, like, arch irony, right? They’re like, these are jokes and memes and silly stuff. But you can’t, like, pull a gun on somebody and force them into a concentration camp in a joking way. And they tried. They really did try. Like, ICE and DHS were putting out all these memes. They had, like, the cartoon meme of the woman crying as she was getting arrested and stuff. But it’s not funny. It’s not funny, because that’s a real person. Like, I think for normal people that voted for Trump—they lied, a lot of people allowed themselves to believe it really was just jokes, that the Haitians eating cats and dogs thing was just a joke. No, they meant that. They meant that in the same way that Nazis saying similar things about Jews meant it. And there becomes the moment where the proof starts to happen that they meant it. And that clip about Donald Trump leading a bunch of people chanting “deport”—like, those are real people. Now, they were always real people, but I think in a lot of people’s imaginations that was a joke. And now you cannot deny that they are actually uprooting these people and sending them to a violent country that they were trying to escape. Sargent: And if you think about the videos that just absolutely saturated the culture, saturated social media, of the shooting of first Renata Good and then second Alex Pretti—in the Renata Good one especially, you could hear the crack of gunfire. You could hear the shots. And those break through all the memes and all the cartoon stuff and all the hilarity and all that sort of stuff. And then the car just sort of slowly rolling down the road with a dead person slumped over the steering wheel, and then essentially hitting a pole. Like, that just broke the memes, I think. Marcotte: Yeah. It’s very reminiscent of how a lot of the Black Lives Matter protests rose up out of seeing video of people getting killed by police. And you know, that has a clarifying effect on the mind. Because yeah, now it’s not a cartoon anymore. That’s a person. That person has a family, you know. Sargent: Yeah. Well, just to completely wrap this up, where do you see this going? You’ve got Trump doing these rallies. He’s obviously struggling to boost energy in MAGA country. I fear it’s going to be a little bit successful. Like, they are going to bring Republicans back into the fold, especially because they’re going to outspend Democrats by around $200 million or something. And we’re going to see potentially the polls tighten. I think people should be prepared for that. Marcotte: I cannot emphasize enough how much, in some communities in this country, the idea of voting for a Democrat is the equivalent of selling your child into slavery. It’s treated as—they are literally told that it’s demonic, that you will literally go to hell if you vote for a Democrat. And so I think a lot of people are going to struggle to do that, even though they know in their heart that it’s the right thing to do. So yeah, I think a lot of them, if they go to the voting booth, I think they’re going to vote for the Republican. That said, they’re going to have a turnout problem. I think a lot of people aren’t going to want to make that choice. And so they’re probably just going to sit this one out. Sargent: Yep. It sure looks like it’s trending in the right direction. Amanda Marcotte, always awesome to talk to you. Thanks so much. Marcotte: Thanks for having me.

World: Epidemic and emerging disease alerts in the Pacific as of 06 October 2026
articles.description: Countries: World, Australia, Fiji, Guam, Marshall Islands, Micronesia (Federated States of), New Caledonia (France), New Zealand, Niue (New Zealand), Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis and Futuna (France) Source: Pacific Community Please refer to the attached Map. Highlights/updates since the last map was sent on PacNet on 29 September 2026: Dengue • Marshall Islands: The 10th Outbreak Situation Report on dengue in Majuro and Ebeye, dated 28 September 2026 and covering 15 August to 25 September, records 297 specimens tested (Majuro 263, Ebeye 34) and 112 confirmed positive (Majuro 97, Ebeye 15), with no deaths and seven cumulative hospitalisations. Four cases had onset in the past seven days (Majuro 3, Ebeye 1). The confirmed-case attack rate is 4.2 per 1,000 in Majuro and 1.5 per 1,000 in Ebeye, and the Majuro positivity rate is 36.8 percent. Only DENV-1 has been detected. The red alert for dengue (DENV-1) remains in effect. – Source: Republic of the Marshall Islands Ministry of Health and Human Services, Outbreak of Dengue Fever Cases in Majuro & Ebeye, 10th Outbreak Situation Report shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 01 October 2026. • Samoa: The Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 76 for EpiWeek 39 (21 to 27 September 2026) reports 35 new cases, a 169 percent increase on the previous week, including five laboratory-confirmed cases, against one the week before. Two new admissions and no deaths were reported. Since 1 January 2025, 20,308 clinically diagnosed cases, 5,546 laboratory-confirmed cases and nine dengue-related deaths have been recorded. DENV-1 accounts for 52 percent and DENV-2 for 48 percent of serotyped cases, and children under 15 years for 73 percent of cases. The outbreak will be declared over after 28 days without a new laboratory-confirmed case. The blue alert for dengue (DENV-1 & DENV-2) remains in effect. – Source: Ministry of Health Samoa, Dengue Fever Outbreak Situation Report Issue No. 76, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 06 October 2026. • Vanuatu: Situation Report #14 on the dengue outbreak on Efate and Santo, dated 28 September 2026, reports 17 new laboratory-confirmed cases in EpiWeeks 38 and 39 (14 to 27 September), 10 from Efate and 7 from Santo, bringing the cumulative total to 169 confirmed cases. Weekly numbers remain above the outbreak threshold of four confirmed cases per week, although they have declined since the peak of EpiWeeks 33 to 35. In Santo, cases are now reported in Luganville, East Santo and Canal-Fanafo Area Councils. Sixteen dengue-associated hospitalisations have been reported, all discharged, with no severe dengue and no deaths. DENV-1 remains the only serotype detected. Tafea Provincial Health has also declared a dengue outbreak in Tafea Province, and its response team is investigating cases, tracing contacts and raising community awareness in the West Tanna Area Council. The red alert for dengue (DENV-1) remains in effect for Vanuatu. – Sources: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Dengue Outbreak on Efate and Santo Island, Situation Report #14, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 1st October 2026, Official dengue press released for Tanna - Tafea Health Promotion official Facebook page and Tafea Provincial Health, Dengue response West Tanna accessed on 06 October 2026. • Wallis and Futuna: The Health Agency reported on 1st October 2026 that the dengue epidemic is continuing, with 11 new confirmed cases over weeks 37 to 39, four on Wallis and seven on Futuna, bringing the cumulative total for the territory to 95 confirmed or probable cases. The red alert for dengue remains in effect for Wallis and Futuna. – Source: Agence de Santé de Wallis et Futuna, epidemiological and health watch update for weeks 37 to 39 (1st October 2026) shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 06 October 2026. Measles • Australia: NSW Health issued a measles alert for the Campbelltown area on 03 October 2026 after a confirmed case in a returned traveller from South-East Asia. While infectious, the person visited several sites in the Campbelltown area and locations in Concord and Rooty Hill. As of 06 October 2026, 119 measles notifications have been reported nationally in Australia in 2026, already exceeding the annual totals for each year from 2020 to 2024 (25, 0, 7, 26 and 57 respectively), following 181 notifications in 2025, the highest annual count since 2019 (285). In 2026, New South Wales has reported the largest number of notifications (n=55), followed by Victoria (n=30), Queensland (n=18), South Australia (n=9), Western Australia (n=5) and the Australian Capital Territory (n=2). No cases have been notified in the Northern Territory or Tasmania. The red alert for measles remains in effect for Australia. – Sources: NSW Health, Measles alert for Campbelltown area and National Notifiable Disease Surveillance Syestem - Australian Centre fo Disease Control accessed on 5 October 2026. • Papua New Guinea: The National Department of Health weekly bulletin for EpiWeek 39 (21 to 27 September 2026) reports 17 laboratory-confirmed measles cases in 2026, up from 13 the previous week: National Capital District 6, East Sepik 4, Western Highlands 2, and one each in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, Eastern Highlands, Enga and New Ireland. The last onset date is 15 September 2026. Rubella cases rose from 21 to 25, and ten patients are positive for both measles and rubella. Year to date, 361 acute fever and rash cases have been reported and 373 samples submitted. The measles-rubella vaccination campaign targets all children under seven in districts with a detected case. The red alert for measles remains in effect for Papua New Guinea. – Source: Papua New Guinea National Department of Health, Public Health Events Weekly Bulletin, EpiWeek 39 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 02 October 2026. Pertussis • Vanuatu: Situation Report 05 on the pertussis outbreak in Penama Province, dated 28 September 2026, reports 21 new cases on Ambae Island in EpiWeeks 38 and 39 (respectively 1 and 20), bringing the cumulative total to 605 cases, of which 4 are laboratory confirmed. The outbreak peaked in EpiWeeks 36 and 37 (266 and 307 clinically diagnosed cases) and case numbers have since declined substantially, but continued detection shows that community transmission has not been interrupted. Two cases have been hospitalised since the start of the outbreak and no death is reported. North Ambae accounts for 54 percent of cases and South Ambae for 43 percent. The red alert for pertussis remains in effect for Vanuatu. – Source: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Pertussis Outbreak in Penama Province, Situation Report 5 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 01 October 2026. Respiratory diseases • New Caledonia: The Directorate of Health and Social Affairs (DASS) announced on 1st October 2026 that New Caledonia has entered an influenza epidemic phase. In week 39 (21 to 27 September), 115 new laboratory-confirmed cases were recorded, bringing the 2026 total to 238, 190 of them since week 33. A/H1N1pdm09 predominates and laboratory positivity reached 56 percent. Acute respiratory infections exceeded 15 percent of sentinel GP consultations in weeks 38 and 39. In week 39, 221 emergency department presentations were for acute respiratory infection (12 percent of all presentations, against 4 percent in week 37) and 54 patients were hospitalised, with a median age of 71 years. Since 27 September, bed occupancy in intensive care and continuous monitoring units has exceeded 75 percent. People aged 65 and over account for 36 percent of confirmed cases. The epidemic comes earlier than in 2024 and 2025. A red alert for influenza A is issued for New Caledonia. – Source: Direction des Affaires Sanitaires et Sociales de Nouvelle-Calédonie, Vigilance DASS bulletin 2026-#08, influenza epidemic, shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 02 October 2026. • New Zealand: For the week ending 27 September 2026, the all-cause SARI hospitalisation rate in the Auckland region has decreased into the low activity band, and the influenza-positive SARI rate decreased for the fourth week in a row and is now low. Influenza remained the most commonly detected virus among SARI patients, with test positivity stable at 32.9 percent, while positivity among sentinel GP influenza-like illness cases fell from 34.3 to 27.3 percent. A/H1 and A/H3 are detected at similar levels. Twenty-eight influenza-positive SARI patients have been admitted to intensive care in 2026, all since 27 July. Since 1st January, 5,296 influenza-positive specimens have been reported nationally (4,912 influenza A and 384 influenza B), and circulating viruses match the 2026 vaccine. Pacific peoples have had the highest cumulative rates of influenza-, RSV- and SARS-CoV-2-positive SARI hospitalisation in 2026. The red alert for influenza A is changed to a blue alert for New Zealand. – Sources: PHF Science, New Zealand Acute Respiratory Illness dashboard , accessed on 5 October 2026 and PHF Science, Virology Weekly Report, week 39, accessed on 5 October 2026. Rotavirus • Federated States of Micronesia: Situation Reports #18 and #19 on the diarrhoeal outbreak in Yap State, dated 25 September and 1st October 2026, report one new case on 25 September and nine between 28 September and 1st October, two of them from Ifalik Dispensary in the Outer Islands, bringing the cumulative total to 240. There have been 14 admissions since the outbreak began, 12 of them children, and no deaths. Rotavirus remains predominant, mostly as co-infections with E. coli , adenovirus, Salmonella , Giardia and, newly, Clostridioides difficile , and a laboratory-confirmed rotavirus reinfection was detected in a two-year-old. Children aged 0 to 11 years account for 66 percent of cases. Case counts have declined to low single digits since mid-September but remain above the alert threshold. The red alert for rotavirus is changed to a blue alert for the Federated States of Micronesia (Yap State). – Source: Yap State Diarrhoeal Outbreak Situation Reports #18 and #19 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 29 September and 02 October 2026. • Vanuatu: Situation Report No. 6 on the rotavirus outbreak in Tafea Province, dated 30 September 2026, reports 123 acute watery diarrhoea cases in EpiWeek 39 (21 to 27 September), bringing the cumulative total to 1,140 cases, three of them laboratory confirmed. Case numbers declined in EpiWeeks 38 and 39 but remain above the alert threshold of 34 cases per week. Cases have been reported on Aneityum Island for the first time, with 12 cases in EpiWeek 39. Children under five account for most cases. A total of 44 patients have been hospitalised since EpiWeek 33 and one death, in a one-year-old child, was reported in EpiWeek 35. Water testing detected E. coli contamination. The Ministry of Health has also declared a rotavirus outbreak in Sanma Province, on Santo, where more than 100 acute watery diarrhoea cases were reported between 24 August and 20 September and four confirmed cases in the latest week met the declaration criteria. The red alert for rotavirus remains in effect for Vanuatu. – Sources: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Rotavirus Outbreak in Tanna and Aneityum Island, Situation Report No. 6 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 01 October 2026 and Vanuatu Daily Post, Water diarrhoea outbreak on Santo , accessed on 03 October 2026. Other Information: One Health - High pathogenicity avian influenza • Australia: The national H5 bird flu dashboard recorded 682 confirmed events in wildlife as of 02 October 2026, against 652 on 25 September: South Australia 325, Victoria 230, New South Wales 68, Tasmania 46, Western Australia 10, Queensland 2 and Jervis Bay Territory 1. H5 has not been reported from any Pacific Island country or territory to date . – Source: Australian Government Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry, H5 bird flu latest data accessed on 05 October 2026. • Pacific Island countries and areas: The WHO Western Pacific Region Avian Influenza Weekly Update No. 1064 (02 October 2026) presents a rapid joint One Health risk assessment of high pathogenicity avian influenza incursion into Pacific Island countries and areas. Following detections of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in Australia and New Zealand, entry through seabird and wild bird movements in the south-west Pacific is assessed as very high risk from August 2026 to January 2027, and entry through poultry trade and human movement as low. If introduced, establishment would be high risk in resident wild birds and very high risk in domestic poultry, given free-ranging backyard poultry and limited biosecurity. Human exposure is assessed as low under current conditions. No human avian influenza case was reported in the Region. – Source: WHO Western Pacific Region, Avian Influenza Weekly Update No. 1064 accessed on 06 October 2026. Respiratory diseases • Guam: The Communicable Disease Surveillance Dashboard, updated on 05 October 2026, shows the late-season influenza wave reaching its highest level of 2026 in EpiWeek 38 with about 151 influenza and influenza-like illness cases, against about 121 the previous week. In EpiWeek 38, there were 62 laboratory-confirmed influenza A cases. All influenza viruses subtyped in August and September were A(H1N1) with 44 percent of cases are aged 5 to 19 years. – Source: Guam Department of Public Health and Social Services, Communicable Disease Surveillance Dashboard accessed on 06 October 2026. • Nauru: The Naoero Medical Centre has observed an ongoing increase in influenza infections, with more people seeking care for influenza-like symptoms, and health authorities urge the public to remain vigilant and take preventive measures. – Source: Nauru health authorities accessed on 06 October 2026. • Niue: The Public Health Snapshot for 22 to 28 September 2026 reports 17 new confirmed influenza A cases, after 24 the previous week, bringing the total to 104 since 17 August 2026. Thirteen hospital admissions, all for influenza A, have been recorded since 17 August. No COVID-19 or influenza B case was reported. – Source: Niue Public Health Division, Public Health Snapshot, 22-28 September 2026 accessed on 06 October 2026. • Palau: The Ministry of Health and Human Services reported on 02 October 2026 a total of 53 influenza A cases in 2026, with activity increasing in recent weeks. – Source: Palau Ministry of Health and Human Services, Respiratory Disease Situational Update accessed on 06 October 2026. • Tonga: The weekly syndromic surveillance report for EpiWeek 39 (21 to 27 September 2026) records 73 influenza-like illness cases, the fifth consecutive weekly increase and the highest weekly count of 2026, with a sharp rise in positive respiratory samples, mostly influenza A. On 05 October, the Ministry of Health issued an influenza A alert asking the public to watch for symptoms, with particular care for children under five, people aged 65 and over, pregnant women and heavy smokers. – Sources: Tonga Ministry of Health, Weekly Communicable Diseases Syndromic Surveillance, EpiWeek 39 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 01 October 2026 and Ministry of Health Tonga accessed on 06 October 2026. • Vanuatu: The Ministry of Health reported on 30 September 2026 that it is closely monitoring increased influenza-like illness activity, particularly in Shefa, Tafea and Penama provinces, where case numbers have remained above provincial alert thresholds in recent weeks. More than 19,000 ILI cases were reported nationally between EpiWeeks 1 and 37 of 2026. No outbreak has been declared. – Source: Vanuatu Ministry of Health, Health Promotion, ILI update accessed on 06 October 2026. • Wallis and Futuna: The Health Agency multi-source surveillance dashboard, updated on 05 October 2026, shows influenza-like illness rising steadily on Wallis since early September, reaching 69 consultations in the week ending of 21 September, the highest weekly level since January but below the alert threshold of 100. The Health Agency's update of 01 October 2026 reports one influenza A case on Wallis in week 39 and two on Futuna in week 40, while rhinovirus (5 cases) and parainfluenza virus 3 (4 cases) have circulated actively on Wallis since week 37, causing mild respiratory infections and bronchiolitis in children. No indicator is above the vigilance thresholds on either island, and increased vigilance for influenza-like illness is advised in the coming weeks. – Sources: Agence de Santé de Wallis et Futuna, multi-source surveillance dashboard accessed on 06 October 2026, and Agence de Santé de Wallis et Futuna, epidemiological and health watch update for weeks 37 to 39 (1st October 2026) shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 06 October 2026. Rotavirus • Tuvalu: Situational Report #9 on the rotavirus outbreak, covering 28 September to 04 October 2026, reports no new laboratory-confirmed case for the past four weeks. The cumulative total unchanged at 30, 28 on Funafuti and two on Nukufetau, the latest confirmed on 03 September. Genotyping confirmed an equine-like G3P[8] rotavirus. Two patients have been hospitalised and discharged, and 25 of the 30 cases are children under 15 years. A total of 389 suspected diarrhoea cases were reported between 04 August and 04 October, and weekly numbers have returned within the normal threshold. – Source: Tuvalu Ministry of Health, Outbreak of Rotavirus in Tuvalu, Situational Report #9 shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 06 October 2026. • Wallis and Futuna: The Health Agency reported on 1st October 2026 that diarrhoeal syndromes on Wallis have been increasing since week 36 and have exceeded the vigilance threshold for three consecutive weeks, with four rotavirus cases reported. – Source: Agence de Santé de Wallis et Futuna, epidemiological and health watch update for weeks 37 to 39 (1st October 2026), shared with the PPHSN Coordinating Body Focal point on 06 October 2026.

articles.title: Colombia - Key Message Update (September 2026 - January 2027): Negative impacts to livelihoods persist amid erratic rainfall and earthquake aftereffects
articles.description: Country: Colombia Source: Famine Early Warning System Network Please refer to the attached file. Key Messages Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes are likely to continue through January 2027 in La Guajira and Chocó; Stressed (IPC Phase 2) outcomes remain most likely in much of the rest of the country. In La Guajira, deepening rainfall and soil moisture deficits are constraining water access and agricultural and livestock production, resulting in widespread food consumption gaps among poor Indigenous and agropastoral households. In Chocó, poor households in earthquake-affected areas are increasingly relying on unsustainable coping strategies in the face of substantial asset losses and disruptions to livelihoods and markets, while many poor Indigenous and Afro-Colombian households in remote riverine areas continue to struggle with adequate food access due to high transportation costs and intermittent restrictions on movement, access to markets, and livelihoods. In the rest of the country, while pockets of households in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) are expected to persist, most poor households are likely to be able to sustain minimally adequate diets. However, constrained incomes and persistently high prices are expected to limit their ability to meet other essential household needs. In September, broadly below-average rainfall and above-average temperatures associated with El Niño triggered an expansion of areas facing agricultural stress , particularly in La Guajira, Cesar, Atlántico, Tolima, Cundinamarca, and Casanare. In La Guajira, hot and dry conditions are reducing water and pasture availability, limiting yields, and weakening livestock productivity, while declining river levels , elevated wildfire risk , localized flooding from short, intense precipitation events , and forecast well-above-average temperatures , are expected to cause localized agricultural losses and reduced wild food availability elsewhere in Colombia, including in the Amazon, most severely impacting rural communities that rely on subsistence production. While government-led earthquake reconstruction efforts have begun, recovery has been slow and variable for the more than 778,000 people affected , particularly in Chocó, Valle del Cauca, Risaralda, and Quindío. In rural Chocó, livelihood disruptions and asset losses have led to widening food consumption gaps among the worst-affected poor households, especially in Afro-Colombian communities that already face more limited food access due to weather- and/or conflict-related shocks. In urban areas, loss of dwellings and livelihoods has increased the number of households experiencing Crisis (IPC Phase 3) and Stressed (IPC Phase 2) outcomes, since worst-affected households have expanded use of both sustainable and unsustainable coping strategies to reduce or close food consumption gaps as incomes have dropped substantially and expenditures on non-food essentials increased. In relatively better-off departments such as Valle del Cauca, Risaralda, and Quindío, negative impacts to income and assets have deteriorated coping capacity among some previously food-secure populations. Through August, rising and highly variable food prices continued to contribute to increased annual headline inflation, which reached 6.24 percent. Key staple prices remained relatively stable in August: In Bogotá, rice was broadly stable and slightly below both last year and the five-year average, while maize meal and pasta declined slightly month-on-month but remained moderately above their five-year averages. While a relatively strong Colombian peso has partly mitigated import costs for agricultural inputs and grains, domestic food price dynamics are increasingly driven by product- and region-specific weather shocks and resulting supply constraints, exacerbated by increased transportation costs. Rainfall anomalies have severely reduced yields for certain crops and limited pasture regeneration, driving up the cost of items such as green beans, which increased 84.39 percent year-on-year in Cúcuta, and local cheese ( queso costeño ), which saw price increases across 24 major wholesale markets. Significant regional price disparity also persisted, reflecting differences in proximity to harvesting hubs, varying supply chain lengths, and localized weather impacts; for example, year-to-date mango prices surged over 400 percent in Medellín while remaining stable in Barranquilla. In contrast, seasonal harvests supported temporary price declines for some items, including carrots. In conflict-affected areas, particularly in areas linked to illicit economies, intermittent displacement, confinement, and movement restrictions are expected to continue disrupting trade, agricultural activities, and access to informal income sources, resulting in pockets of households in Crisis (IPC Phase 3). In Chocó , Antioquia , and southern Bolívar , armed confrontations, insecurity, and intermittent disruptions to transportation networks will continue to limit access to markets, agricultural fields, and income-generating activities among poor households, including in Afro-Colombian communities. As the new administration continues to reshape security policy and intensifies operations against organized armed groups (OAGs), state forces remain likely to sustain pressure on OAG structures . In response, retaliatory actions by OAGs, including attacks using explosive drones or improvised explosive devices , are expected to persist in affected areas.

articles.title: Agreement to transition away from fossil fuels ‘not open for renegotiation’, Pacific leader tells pre-Cop
articles.description: International leaders visit Tuvalu as part of climate talks co-hosted by Australia ahead of Cop31 conference Pacific island leaders have urged a promised global transition away from fossil fuels must not be left open to renegotiation as they gather in tiny Tuvalu in a bid to build momentum before a major climate summit. About 50 dignitaries – 14 national heads including Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, a list of climate change ministers and the heads of global agencies – flew to the low-lying atoll nation in a bid to bring attention to the plight of the countries most at risk from the climate crisis. articles.title: Horoscope for Tuesday, October 06, 2026
articles.description: Moon Alert Caution! Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 5 a.m. to 10:15 p.m. After that, the moon moves from Leo into Virgo. Aries (March 21-April 19) A dynamic day This is a fantastic day to schmooze, and romance is favored. In fact, this is the most romantic day of the week. Intimate relationships will be affectionate and exciting. Enjoy socializing, sports events and fun activities with kids. The arts are blessed. Taurus (April 20-May 20) A positive day Many of you are excellent cooks, and today is a wonderful day to entertain at home. (It will please you to make a partner, spouse or someone close to you happy.) Discussions about real estate, expanding your family, or contemplating a future vacation will appeal. Gemini (May 21-June 20) A dynamic day This is a feel-good day! You're in a positive frame of mind and ready to entertain big ideas because your confidence is strong. Colleagues at work might endorse your plans. (See moon alert.) Meanwhile, a work-related romance might be percolating on the back burner. Cancer (June 21-July 22) A positive day This is a good money day for you. Jot down your money-making ideas but wait until tomorrow to act on them because today is a moon alert. Nevertheless, a moon alert is a creative time — just a poor day to spend money. This is a friendly, sociable day and great for romance! Leo (July 23-Aug. 22) A dynamic day You're out there flying your colors today because the moon is lined up with lucky Jupiter in Leo. Plus, fiery Mars in your sign will put a spring in your step and boost your confidence. Family discussions will go well. In fact, you might want to entertain at home. Romance is blessed. Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22) A positive day Your ability to charm others with your words is wonderful today, which is why this is a great day for those in marketing, teaching and acting. However, because of the moon alert all day, restrict your own spending to food and gas. Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22) A dynamic day Enjoy your popularity today because everyone wants to see your face! Interactions with friends, groups and organizations will be successful. However, because there's a moon alert all day, don't volunteer for anything. Wait until tomorrow. Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21) An average day You're still high-viz today, which means people notice you more than usual — and you look capable and affluent to everyone. You're also charming and diplomatic. You might be approached to take on increased responsibilities today; if so, wait until tomorrow to accept. (Check Moon Alert.) Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21) A dynamic day This is a fabulous day to travel because you want to get out of Dodge. Meanwhile, some of you might be dabbling in a secret love affair. It's certainly a great day to schmooze and flirt. However, it's a poor day to spend money except for food and gas. (Check moon alert.) Capricorn (Dec. 22-Jan. 19) An average day Be careful with financial issues and decisions today, especially concerning shared property, insurance issues, inheritances, taxes and debt, because there's a moon alert all day. Be smart and postpone these decisions until tomorrow. Forewarned is forearmed. Aquarius (Jan. 20-Feb. 18) A positive day Great day to schmooze! Enjoy the company of friends, partners and spouses because you make such a great impression on everyone. It's possible you'll be asked for your advice about something. If so, wait until tomorrow to respond. See moon alert above. Pisces (Feb. 19-March 20) An average day Work-related travel might be on the menu today. Likewise, travel plans will intrigue you. Although you can be productive today, be aware of the restrictions of the moon alert and postpone important decisions until tomorrow. You'll be glad you did. If today is your birthday Actress Elisabeth Shue (1963) shares your birthday today. You have a strong zest for living. You're optimistic, enthusiastic, and progressive. This year you will attain power and leadership. You will also reap the benefits and rewards for all your hard work. It's a busy year. Expect kudos, awards, promotions and acknowledgment. Seize opportunities that arise.
